items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Clever King' only in the interviewer's question. The interviewee's response discusses arranging for other musicians (Elmer Kaiser, Giron, Carlin, Dan Russo, Charlie Strait) but does not mention Clever King or any interaction with them.

ctx.x: Well, it was, yes, it was a regular dance hall band. It wasn't a jazz band, it was a dance hall band. But when I bought these arrangements up there, they got a big kick out. Then I made some of my own. By studying Duke style and some of the other guys, I began to develop a little bit myself. And I progressed from that straight. And I started to be known as an arrangement.
What were some of the things it is for Clever King? Do you recall that?

Oh, well, I made, I made, I think I made the first arrangement of Rapson in blue around here. First dance arrangement of Rapson in blue. I remember that because we got lots and lots of compliments. And Elmer Kaiser came in and played against us one night and he wanted to know who made the arrangements, so I did. And so I turned around and copied off the score and sold him an arrangement.
